_enforcement_note: block: refuse the tool call and explain. warn: allow but inject the reason as feedback. There is no agent-controlled off mode; policy controls are security boundaries and can only be changed in repository source under review.

bounded_output._note: Project directive: fetch at most 30 lines per call, then request the next 30. A read command must carry an explicit bound (head -N, tail -N, sed -n 'a,bp', grep -m N, git log -n N, --max-count) with N <= max_declared_lines. When the bound is satisfied the output is returned normally; when it is not, the only thing that leaves the hook is refusal_message.
bounded_output._exempt_note: Commands whose output is either trivially small or whose own tooling already bounds it (pytest -q, ruff, git with -n). Exemption applies to the FIRST word of a pipeline segment only; a pipeline that ends in an unbounded reader is still checked.
bounded_output._subcommand_note: Commands that are exempt as a whole but have subcommands whose output is unbounded. `git` is exempt so that `git status` and `git add` are not nagged, but `git log` with no -n can page thousands of commits into context.
bounded_output._oversized_note: A bound that is present but large is not a bound. head -100 puts 100 lines in context just as surely as cat does. These patterns extract the declared N and compare it against max_declared_lines; sed ranges are compared by span.
bounded_output._byte_note: head -c is a legitimate bound for output with no newlines, but a byte bound is still a bound: -c 500000 is unbounded in practice. Compared against max_declared_bytes rather than max_declared_lines.
bounded_output._count_note: grep -c emits a single count line, so it is inherently bounded and must not be treated as an unbounded read just because it follows a reader in the pipeline.
bounded_output.refusal_message: only <=30 lines are allowed,run command for minimum line which can make you understand the failure
bounded_output._gh_note: `gh` is not exempt as a whole, but `gh run view --log`, `gh run list` and `gh api .../logs` page an entire CI run into context. They are allowed only behind an explicit bound; `gh pr view/checks/merge` are untouched.

observation_boundary.read_refusal_message: Read operations must declare a bounded range of at most 30 lines. Use a targeted search first, then request the smallest exact range needed. The returned model observation is additionally compacted to at most three useful lines.
observation_boundary._note: This is a model-context boundary, not a filesystem access control. PostToolUse compacts every successful tool result; PreToolUse prevents unbounded native source reads and direct CI run-data access.

destructive._note: Destructive commands are refused outright. They are not blocked because they are forbidden -- they are blocked because they must be run through common/shell_exec.run() with classification='destructive' and confirm_destructive=True, which records the authorization. The hook names that path in its refusal.
destructive._allow_marker_note: Prefixing a command with this marker documents that a human authorized this specific irreversible action. The marker is deliberately noisy so it cannot be added by habit.

secret_echo._note: Refuse commands that would print a credential store straight into the transcript, which is how a secret ends up in an LLM context and in the session log.

ci_observability._note: Permanent, not situational. CI live-monitoring -- following a run, watching checks, or a poll loop -- streams an unbounded and open-ended amount of build output into context, and no per-call line bound can cap something that never ends. Bulk retrieval is no longer a bounded alternative either: see ci_log_access, which refuses it outright.
ci_observability.message: CI live monitoring and direct CI run-data retrieval are permanently disabled as model-observation routes. Use only python3 scripts/local_checks.py prepare to retrieve the single current-head CI notice.
CI live monitoring and direct CI run-data retrieval are blocked. Use only ./scripts/prfail --pr <PR_NUMBER> for the finalized filtered report.
ci_observability._banned_tools_note: The Monitor tool is a live watch by construction, so it is refused for this project regardless of what it is pointed at.

ci_log_access._note: CI records are never read by an agent. The workflow .github/workflows/ci-failure-notify.yml summarizes one actionable non-green check in one mutable PR comment, bound to the exact head SHA. The only agent-facing subscription is local_checks.py prepare, which returns only that current SHA-bound notice.
ci_log_access.message: CI logs, job records, annotations, artifacts, check results and arbitrary PR comments are blocked. Use only python3 scripts/local_checks.py prepare, which returns the single CI notice whose hidden SHA marker matches HEAD.
ci_log_access._hard_deny_note: Check-result reads are blocked before any comment exception. Direct PR-comment reads are also blocked; only the exact SHA-filtered local_checks.py prepare command is allowed.
ci_log_access._note: The sole agent-facing CI route is ./scripts/prfail --pr <PR_NUMBER>. The collector in .github/workflows/ci-diagnostics.yml publishes a filtered Check Run report bound to the current PR head SHA; all direct Actions data, annotations, logs, artifacts, check results, and legacy PR-comment reads are blocked.
ci_log_access.message: THAPPAR — CI DIAGNOSTIC ACCESS BLOCKED. Use only: ./scripts/prfail --pr <PR_NUMBER>. Direct or alternative diagnostic retrieval is prohibited.
ci_log_access._hard_deny_note: Raw check/log reads are denied before the allowlist. Only the exact ./scripts/prfail --pr positive-decimal command is exempt; selectors and shell wrappers are not implemented.
ci_log_access._allowed_note: Only the exact local notice-preparation command is exempt; direct PR/comment API reads would expose unrelated comments and are blocked.
allowed_patterns._allowed_note: Exactly one command is permitted: ./scripts/prfail --pr followed by a positive decimal PR number.
allowed_patterns._banned_note: Mirrors common.command_schema.CI_LOG_PATTERNS; tests require the shared classifier and JSON fallback to agree.

local_checks.run_command: DISABLED: GitHub Actions is the sole test/build/check execution path.
local_checks.rule: GitHub Actions is the sole execution path for tests, builds, lint, security scans, workflow validation, and quality gates. The only local-check operation permitted is the exact read-only python3 scripts/local_checks.py prepare command, which retrieves only the current HEAD's SHA-bound CI notice. The run subcommand is disabled.
local_checks.run_command: DISABLED: GitHub Actions is the sole test/build/check execution path.
local_checks.rule: GitHub Actions is the sole execution path for tests, builds, lint, security scans, workflow validation, and quality gates. The legacy local_checks.py prepare notice reader is retired for agent use. The only permitted diagnostic retrieval command is ./scripts/prfail --pr <PR_NUMBER>, which reads the finalized filtered Check Run report; the run subcommand remains disabled.

ci_log_access._gh_note: gh is not exempt as a whole. CI run data and arbitrary PR comment reads are blocked; the only permitted comment route is the SHA-filtered local_checks.py prepare command. Ordinary PR metadata and PR comment writes remain separately governed.

CI run data and arbitrary PR-comment reads are blocked. The only permitted diagnostic route is the exact ./scripts/prfail --pr <PR_NUMBER> command; ordinary PR metadata and comment writes remain separately governed.

github_route._note: The GitHub tool contract is code-owned. This section is documentary; it cannot widen a route.
